question: What is the first exact reader of the 64-bit value stored at frame-timing owner +0x10?

scope.boundary: Both accepted writers count toward the eight-function total. The primary global exposes 28 distinct reader functions before field classification, so no read candidate body is selected or inspected.

dependencies.use: Provides the accepted dual publication, +0x10 field, two writers, and timing-owner vtable.

ownerReferenceResult.result: The 28-function primary-owner reader set exceeds the six-candidate cap before any +0x10 reader body can be selected.

boundedNegative.result: No first +0x10 reader is promoted because the accepted owner carriers expose 28 distinct reader functions, exceeding the six-candidate cap. Choosing a subset would not establish first-reader ownership.
boundedNegative.effect: The two exact +0x10 writers remain confirmed, while read ownership and immediate use remain unresolved.
boundedNegative.falsificationCondition: An independently anchored owner consumer or a bounded discriminator reduces the direct reader set to at most six functions and proves an exact +0x10 read.

catalogPromotion.result: The existing +0x10 field gains the over-cap reader qualification; no consumer relation is added.

currentEvidence.method: Three sequential foreground read-only Ghidra queries: exact writer bodies, exact references to both owner globals, and depth-zero WRITE classification for +0x10 in the two writers.
currentEvidence.qualification: No reader candidate was decompiled or field-scanned after the over-cap stop. Split-address consumers and dynamic uses remain outside the direct-reference set.

guards: Do not choose an arbitrary six-reader subset and call it first.
Do not infer that every owner-global reader accesses +0x10.
Do not assign time units, cadence, delta or absolute meaning, frame-rate semantics, or runtime behavior.
conclusion: Both accepted +0x10 stores are reconfirmed, but the primary owner global has 28 distinct reader functions. That exceeds the six-candidate cap, so no first reader or immediate arithmetic/comparison use is promoted.
